brief: Goldman's EU index vol desk reports European spot roughly unchanged on Friday and lower on the week (SXXP -0.81%), with the tape driven by climbing oil and refined products (CO1 +7.80%, XBA +5.39%) and global sovereign yields at new cycle highs rather than by earnings or Fed speak. NFP printed 4 SD above consensus with positive revisions, which moved September hike odds from 50 to 62%, and CPI next week is framed as the more pivotal print. Against that backdrop index vol compressed aggressively, most violently in the belly of the curve, with the SX5E 15 day ATM fixed strike move one of the largest in recent years despite no stressed environment. Luey reads the 1 year pressure as more SPX driven in an illiquid summer tape and questions whether it is rational, since 1y1y is treated as a recession proxy and recession looks unlikely with AI capex intact, while softer high beta vol cuts relative index vol demand. On flows, discretionary nets sub 10th percentile leave room for re-risking, CTAs are long at the 84th percentile and sell 1-2% lower, and buybacks at 1.3x ADTV fade into the ~15 September blackout.
